description: Capture routing for the screenshot library. Splits the 13 manifest shots into the ones the automated harness can produce (Playwright driving code-server in Docker → real webview DOM) and the ones that must be hand-captured from the desktop editor. Consumed by tools/capture/capture.mjs (--plan / capture) and guarded by tests/capture-set.test.mjs. The id set must equal assets/img/screenshots/manifest.json.

shots.open: run `ADO Code: Focus Chat` (adoCode.chat.focus), then send "Plan AB#502"
shots.settle: an assistant message with the `## Plan — AB#502` heading is rendered

shots.open: run `ADO Code: Focus Chat`, send a prompt; the mock replies with a run_terminal_command tool call
run `ADO Code: Focus Chat`, send a prompt; the mock reports the gates green and the PR opened
shots.settle: an assistant message mentioning the created pull request is rendered

shots.open: run `ADO Code: Focus Chat`, send "run the verification gates"
shots.settle: an assistant message with the tests / lint / build gate summary is rendered

shots.open: run `ADO Code: Focus Chat`, then click `.mode-toggle` in the input toolbar
shots.settle: the mode menu (Ask / Plan / Agent / Auto) is open

shots.open: run `ADO Code: Focus Chat`, send "draw the checkout flow"; the mock replies with a mermaid fence
shots.settle: the inline Mermaid diagram renders (svg inside `.markdown-body`)

shots.open: run `ADO Code: Configuration…` (adoCode.openSettings) on the MCP/Skills tab
shots.settle: the MCP server list (`.config-mcp`) shows the connected demo servers, or the skills catalog renders

shots.open: select work item 502 (`ADO Code: Select Work Item`), then run `ADO Code: Show Full Details`
shots.settle: the work item detail webview shows the description, acceptance criteria and discussion
shots.note: Most fragile scene: `Show Full Details` needs a selected work item, and selection goes through a native QuickPick. If it proves unreliable in the web shell, hand-capture this shot.

shots.reason: Tree views are virtualised native workbench chrome; code-server's web shell does not render their rows faithfully (no real explorer styling, different scroll model).
shots.how: Desktop VS Code with the demo org connected: expand Epic → Feature → Story → Task in the ADO Code work items view, 1440x900 @2x.

shots.reason: The QuickPick is native workbench chrome, not a webview; the web shell renders it differently (and it is the surface we need pixel-accurate).
shots.how: Desktop VS Code: Ctrl+Shift+P, type `ADO Code:`, screenshot the palette.

shots.reason: The run card lives in the native worktrees tree, and it only appears after a real delegated run creates a worktree — neither is reproducible from a static render.
shots.how: Desktop VS Code: delegate a task so a worktree is created, expand the ADO Code worktrees view, capture the run card.

shots.reason: `ADO Code: Show Memory` opens a native QuickPick of stored entries and the memory scopes also render as rows in the native status tree; there is no memory webview, so the browser route cannot produce this shot.
shots.how: Desktop VS Code: add a user + workspace memory entry, run `ADO Code: Show Memory`, capture the QuickPick listing both scopes.

shots.reason: The To-do view is native workbench chrome: real tree rows with checkboxes, status icons and a per-session badge. code-server's web shell does not render those rows faithfully, so the harness cannot produce it.
shots.how: Desktop VS Code: set a session goal, let the agent add a few to-do items in different states, then capture the To-do view open in the activity bar.
